item.title: UNLV survives Halloween fright against Northern Illinois
item.description: UNLV Football wide receiver Kayden McGee (6) celebrates a touchdown on the first play of the game during a college football game against the NIU Huskies on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, NV. LAS VEGAS—It was fitting that a Halloween night in Las Vegas would see the football equivalent of a slasher movie play out. Offense was the rule of the night for the UNLV Rebels, who managed to avoid an upset at the hands of a persistent Northern Illinois Huskies team with a 31-24 victory to keep their Mountain West championship hopes alive. The statistic that stands out like a sore thumb is clear to spot: the offenses for both teams were absolute juggernauts. Totaling nearly a thousand yards of total offense between them, UNLV and Northern Illinois wasted no time in getting the ball down the field. Both quarterbacks threw for over 250 yards, and both teams boasted a rusher and receiver who eclipsed the 100-yard mark. It created the sense of a game that was beyond all control, which is never a good feeling for any coach to have. “We made a lot of big plays that we needed to to win the game. We also made a lot of critical errors,” said UNLV head coach Dan Mullen as he critiqued the game in the postgame presser. “As we know, in this conference, its margin for error is really small. You got to play really well every single week and, if you don’t, if you make some critical errors that we made, don’t be shocked with how the game goes and the result of the game.” Needless to say, UNLV defensive coordinator Paul Guenther is going to be a busy man over the next week, particularly in shoring up the run defense. Northern Illinois put up 493 total yards of offense up on the Rebels, including 240 yards on the ground alone. Elijah Porter would lead the Huskies with 113 rushing yards on 21 carries, while Telly Johnson Jr. would add 72 yards and a score on the ground. Coming off of the heels of a game against Air Force where the Rebels gave up 430 rushing yards, the back-to-back weeks of struggles containing the ground game certainly has to be high on the priority list for UNLV as they head into the final month of the regular season. “We got to play better. We got to be better up front defensively,” said Mullen on how they can address the run defense. While the Rebels did have their share of struggles in the passing game (receiver George Dimopoulos finished with 127 yards and a score on seven receptions), UNLV would manage to respond with an aerial attack of their own. Despite throwing two interceptions (one of which on a 50/50 ball that Taz Reddicks was unable to come down with), Rebels quarterback Jackson Arnold was able to put together an efficient outing with 264 passing yards and three touchdowns, as well as adding 86 yards on the ground. The first play of the game was Arnold uncorking a 75-yard shot to Kayden McGee, and the receiver ended the day with 112 yards on four receptions as the Rebels put together a more balanced offense. item.title: Real Madrid summer signing makes emotional admission: ‘I dreamed of this since I was a child’
item.description: Real Madrid summer signing makes emotional admission: ‘I dreamed of this since I was a child’ Real Madrid had a blockbuster summer transfer window, making a number of signings to strengthen the squad at Jose Mourinho’s disposal. The biggest of those signings, undoubtedly, was Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig. The Ivorian winger has already shown glimpses of his enormous potential. After a slow start to life in the Spanish capital, he has come into his own in recent weeks . Diomande opens up about his Real Madrid dream Playing for Los Blancos means much more than just football for the 19-year-old. Speaking in an interview, Diomande explained how this transfer was the fulfilment of a lifelong ambition. “Real Madrid is the transfer I’ve dreamed of since I was a child, and it’s hard to find the words to describe what it means to have achieved it,” Diomande admitted (h/t Madrid Zone ). The 19-year-old’s journey to this point has been extraordinary. He received his first major opportunity with Leganes in 2025. Impressive performances for the La Liga club earned him a move to RB Leipzig, where he went on to have a breakthrough season. Yan Diomande has repeatedly shown his willingness to track back and defend. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) One campaign was enough to convince Real Madrid that he was worth spending around €140 million on. Diomande expressed gratitude to both his former clubs for the roles they played in helping him become the player he is. He also admitted that despite achieving his childhood dream, he still misses his friends and family back home. Real Madrid seem to have struck gold It is still early days, but the feeling is that Real Madrid have landed a major coup by signing Yan Diomande. In just a few months, he has already made the team look better when he plays on the left wing than when Vinicius Jr. does. How does Diomande’s role change with the return of Vinicius Jr? (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) One aspect of his game that Jose Mourinho will be a huge fan of is his innate willingness to track back and defend. The Ivorian winger has also started chipping in consistently with goals and assists and looks set to have an important role to play throughout the season. The one concern right now is how the 19-year-old’s prominence changes once Vinicius returns from suspension. It remains to be seen whether Mourinho switches Diomande back to the right wing or uses him in rotation with Vinicius in the important games ahead.

item.title: Back in form, Defensive experiment | Three takeaways from Barcelona 6-1 Deportivo Alaves
item.description: Back in form, Defensive experiment | Three takeaways from Barcelona 6-1 Deportivo Alaves Barcelona returned to winning ways against Deportivo Alaves last night at the Spotify Camp Nou as they dispatched six goals past the Spanish side in grand style. It took Barcelona just eight minutes to get on the scoresheet through Raphinha, and the lead was soon doubled by Fermin Lopez , who scored from a tight angle to make it 2-0. A second goal from Raphinha made the score 3-0 in Barcelona’s favour, and Lamine Yamal then capped off the first half with a fourth goal to put the result beyond doubt. The carnage tapered down after the break, but Yamal completed his brace with a cool finish, and Anthony Gordon added the cherry on top with a neat lob over the goalkeeper, completing the demolition. Barca Universal brings you three takeaways from Barcelona 6-1 Deportivo Alaves. Back in form Back to winning ways. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Barcelona’s win over Deportivo Alaves last night followed the same pattern the team’s games have largely followed over the past two months, as it was one-way traffic in the Catalans’ favor. Despite not racking up as many shots on target as they usually do, Barcelona were very efficient with their chances as they buried six goals while also looking to be in complete control throughout the game. The game was similar to how the season started for Barcelona. Somewhere along the way, they got distracted and fell apart in the two games that mattered most, but they now seem to be back on track. Lamine Yamal was not at his best but still racked up a brace, while Raphinha, who was also not at his best, netted two goals as well. Fermin Lopez played in imperious form and left the game as the man of the match, while Anthony Gordon once again showed that his finishing has become more clinical. In midfield, Pedri and Rodri once again pulled the strings in the first half and took the game away from Alaves before they could settle in. After the break, Marc Bernal replaced Pedri and provided a mature performance. All in all, Barcelona showed that they have bounced back from the two harsh setbacks of the season and are back on song. A positive defensive experiment Brian Farinas shone at right-back. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Faced with an acute defensive crisis ahead of the game, Hansi Flick was forced to be creative with his back line last night, and his starting combination broke the headlines. Instead of handing Alejandro Balde a start when it seemed like there was no other option, the manager played Joao Cancelo at left-back and handed Brian Farinas a start at right-back. Further, it was the captain Frenkie de Jong who joined Pau Cubarsi in central defence to hand Gerard Martin some time off – thereby delivering the second selection surprise. item.title: Hansi Flick talks Yamal, de Jong, Farinas and Gavi after Barcelona 6-1 Alaves
item.description: Hansi Flick talks Yamal, de Jong, Farinas and Gavi after Barcelona 6-1 Alaves After two successive defeats, FC Barcelona returned to winning ways in an emphatic manner, securing a 6-1 victory at home against Deportivo Alaves. It was a dominant display from the Catalans, with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha both bagging a brace while Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon also chipped in with goals. After the game, coach Hansi Flick was quite delighted with Barcelona’s performance on the night , as he talked about some key aspects of the game, including Yamal’s performance, especially after a painful Ballon d’Or snub. Flick hails Yamal and Raphinha Hansi Flick was delighted with the overall performance against a team that can be defensively stubborn. “We played well and were very focused. We knew Alaves would defend well, but we dominated the first half at a high level and the result confirms it ,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Yamal had a solid outing vs Alaves. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) Yamal, who scored twice before being withdrawn, drew a special mention, especially after the youngster was snubbed in the Ballon d’Or gala, as he finished third behind Kylian Mbappe and Harry Kane. “When you score two goals, it’s easier to get substituted. I spoke to him at halftime. He’s regained his confidence and had many one-on-one situations. He played a fantastic match ,” he said. Flick was equally complimentary of his captain, adding: “Lamine and Raphinha were fantastic. We reacted very well and we’re on the right track.” De Jong at centre-back and a debutant shines With his defence ravaged by injuries, Flick turned to an unlikely solution in Frenkie de Jong. “We have many injured defenders and we don’t know when they’ll be back. I asked Frenkie if he could play centre-back and he said yes, that he wanted to help the team ,” he said. There was also high praise for academy product Brian Farinas, who seized his chance. “I’m very happy with his progress. He’s played at a high level and connects very well with Lamine. He deserved these minutes because he trains very well and his attitude is outstanding. That’s exactly what I want from my players.” A personal milestone for Flick The rout coincided with Flick’s 100th win as Barcelona boss – a milestone he could have ideally secured against Real Madrid last weekend. “It’s incredible. First we reached 100 matches and now 100 wins. It’s fantastic ,” he said. De Jong impressed in a centre-back role. item.title: Courtois, Tchouameni to start | Predicted Real Madrid line-up against Racing Club
item.description: Courtois, Tchouameni to start | Predicted Real Madrid line-up against Racing Club Following a much-needed victory in the El Clasico, Real Madrid shifts its focus to Racing Club as the Los Blancos look to extend their winning streak. Jose Mourinho confirmed at the pre-match conference that either Denzel Dumfries or Trent Alexander-Arnold will start, as Fede Valverde continues his recovery following an injury against FC Barcelona. That being said, here is how Real Madrid is expected to line up against Racing Club. Predicted Real Madrid line-up against Racing Club. GK: Thibaut Courtois The Belgian returns to the side after being sidelined just hours before the El Clasico . Andriy Lunin might feel hard done, but it is not easy to bench arguably the best goalkeeper in the world right now. RB: Trent Alexander-Arnold Against a defence that is known for leaking goals, Trent is the best weapon to use. His pinpoint crosses and ability to take corners and indirect free-kicks make him an asset to have in the squad. CB: Ibrahima Konate Barely put a foot wrong against FC Barcelona and has seemingly secured his place as one of the fixed starting centre-backs in the team. CB: Dean Huijsen The Dutch partnered Konate well and together they kept the Barca attack at bay. Jose Mourinho would hope this duo continues their form into this match as well. LB: Marc Cucurella Cucurella showed why the club signed him after a monstrous performance against Lamine Yamal. The 28-year-old would be eager to carry that form forward. CM: Bernardo Silva The Roma match showed why he deserves to start. Expected to keep his place in the line-up. CM: Aurelien Tchouameni He is known to blow hot and cold in his Real Madrid career so far. The Frenchman will look to build on the momentum from his performance against Barcelona. RW: Arda Guler Fair to say, Real Madrid’s creative engine so far? He can create a pass out of nowhere, possesses impeccable vision and oozes class whenever he has played this season. item.title: Racing Club vs Real Madrid: Match preview | La Liga
item.description: Racing Club vs Real Madrid: Match preview | La Liga Another away contest awaits Real Madrid in La Liga as the men in white travel to Santander to take on Racing Club on matchday 11. Los Blancos are fresh off an El Clasico win , which must be the highlight of the 5-match unbeaten streak Jose Mourinho’s men are on. Fede Valverde ruled out; a blessing in disguise for Dumfries or Trent? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Real Madrid captain played 40 minutes in the El Clasico with an injury, and is now confirmed to be ruled out of tonight’s contests in order to focus on his recovery. The Uruguayan’s omission means Trent Alexander-Arnold or Denzel Dumfries have a chance to make a case for themselves and stamp their authority in Fede’s absence. This is set to be the only change to the El Clasico lineup so far, with Bernardo Silva , Arda Guler and Yan Diomande expected to keep their places in the starting XI. Speaking of Diomande, the youngster has seemingly adapted well and rose to prominence in Vinicius’ absence, and tonight will offer him another opportunity to create a selection headache for Mourinho once the Brazilian returns. Kylian Mbappe meanwhile, fresh off a brace against FC Barcelona and a closely fought Ballon d’Or race with Harry Kane, would look to add to his tally against a vulnerable Racing Club side. The newly promoted team currently sit on 15th in the table, just a couple of points from relegation and have conceded 26 goals so far — most in La Liga. Racing, however, will be high on momentum on their side, having won their last two matches. With Real Madrid being on a 5-match winning streak and Racing also securing consecutive victories, this match promises to be an interesting fixture, despite the stark difference in quality; that being said, Los Blancos should not be taking this match lightly.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama issues perfect seven-word response when asked if he should've won MVP last year
item.description: Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC Victor Wembanyama is one of the best players in the NBA, but he has still never won the MVP award. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was named the MVP in each of the last two seasons. Wembanyama, who was amazing last year, ranked third on that list. Many were of the opinion that the San Antonio Spurs star should’ve won it last year, but the 7’4″ superstar’s focus is on the future. Victor Wembanyama responds when asked if he should’ve won MVP last year Wembanyama averaged 25 points, 11.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 64 games in 2025-26. The 22-year-old was picked to play in his second All-Star game and was also named the Defensive Player of the Year. However, Gilgeous-Alexander pipped him to the MVP crown, and Wembanyama looked visibly upset as the OKC Thunder star lifted his award. On 60 Minutes, the Frenchman was asked if he felt that he should’ve won the Most Valuable Player award for his performances in the 2025-26 season. He confidently replied: “I should win it this year, though.” That is the perfect response, as there is absolutely no point in looking back at what has actually happened. His full focus is on this season, and he seems determined to get his hands on the MVP award. So far this season, Wembanyama has averaged 28 points per game, which is higher than any other season in his NBA career. If he keeps it going, his MVP dream could finally come true. item.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow adds to England’s half-back woes
item.description: England ’s half-back problems have deepened with Alex Mitchell a major doubt for their Nations Championship fixtures this month after suffering a hamstring injury. Mitchell was forced off early in the first half of Northampton Saints ’ 28-14 win over Gloucester, with the initial prognosis not positive for involvement in the autumn. Steve Borthwick was already fretting over the fitness of Northampton fly half Fin Smith , who has a calf injury, while McParland suffered an issue in England camp this week. It leaves Jack van Poortvliet likely to retain the starting No 9 shirt for England’s opener against Australia on Sunday, with Smith expected to be given until Wednesday to prove his fitness. “Fin and Archie are both calf [injuries], Fin probably not as bad as Archie, but it remains to be seen,” Phil Dowson, the Northampton director of rugby, said. “Mitchell has hurt his hamstring but I don’t know how bad. We have to be super-careful with Alex.” Mitchell missed the last two rounds of the Six Nations with a hamstring issue, and was also afflicted by an injury in that area towards the back-end of the last Gallagher Prem season. Borthwick will confirm his Nations Championship squad on Monday morning, with Bath hooker Kepu Tuipulotu another major doubt. Bath’s Kepu Tuipulotu is set to see a surgeon (PA Wire) The 21-year-old will see a surgeon about a knee injury sustained in England training. Theo Dan , a possible alternative call-up, also lasted just 10 minutes of Saracens’ win over Newcastle Red Bulls on Saturday. Flanker Guy Pepper and centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg have already been ruled out of the autumn. England face the Wallabies, Japan, New Zealand and a game on the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium. Additional reporting by the Press Association

Philadelphia Phillies star Bryce Harper is bracing for a long offseason, as he does not sound optimistic that the looming MLB lockout will be resolved in time for the 2027 season . The two-time NL MVP dropped the hint on TikTok , replying to a few comments on one of his posts. When one user joked that March through October seems to be the offseason for Harper, the Phillies slugger responded, “It will be this year.” Another user pointed out that Harper appears to like the offseason more than the season, and he simply answered, “This is true.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) His comments come at a tense time for the sport. The collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the players union expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1, and a lockout is widely expected. At the center of the dispute is a salary cap. Owners are making their strongest push for one in decades, proposing a cap of $245.3 million along with a payroll floor of $171.2 million. The players have long opposed a cap, and MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer has made the union’s stance clear . “The fundamental nature of a salary cap is bad for players on multiple levels,” Meyer said in March. Harper has been one of the most outspoken players on the issue. In July 2025, he reportedly told commissioner Rob Manfred to “get the f*** out of our clubhouse” when Manfred brought up a salary cap during a meeting with the Phillies, according to ESPN’s Jeff Passan. In May, Harper urged both sides to find common ground , saying, “We can’t lose that momentum as players. We can’t lose that momentum as owners.” He is not the only one expecting a lengthy fight. USA Today’s Bob Nightingale reported in September that executives believe the 2027 season will not begin until around Memorial Day weekend. For Harper, the time off comes after another early postseason exit. The Phillies were eliminated by the Atlanta Braves in the Wild Card Series, losing 6-2 in Game 3. Harper hit .269 with 29 home runs, 87 RBIs and an .865 OPS during the regular season. The 34-year-old may be enjoying the offseason for now, but if his prediction is right, Phillies fans could be waiting a long time to see him back on the field. item.title: Judge's exhibition shines light on roller skating
item.description: Ellen, 2019, by Debby Besford [DEBBY BESFORD] A national roller skating judge and photographer, who has captured the lives of seven artistic skaters over 10 years, hopes her exhibition can shine a spotlight on the sport - and wishes that one day it will be in the Olympics. Debby Besford grew up in Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, which has a strong roller skating heritage, and travelled all over the country to compete. While flicking through photo albums on a visit to her parents and reminiscing over her skating days, she decided it would be "fantastic" to do an exhibition about young skaters from the town's Retro Skating Academy. She said it was "amazing" to see how skating had shaped their lives during the decade. Megan, 2025, by Debby Besford [DEBBY BESFORD] Besford said roller skating had been "very, very important for many, many years" to Great Yarmouth, with the town producing a number of champions. She said the Victorian Winter Gardens on the seafront, which used to house a prominent rink and is undergoing restoration , was "a place that was like my creative space and my safe space as well, and to have another family of skaters and parents to support you". Over the years she has gained various items of memorabilia, which she is also featuring in her exhibition called The Art of Roller Skating, based at the town's Time and Tide Museum until April. Debby Besford used to skate in Great Yarmouth's Winter Gardens as a young girl in the 1980s [DEBBY BESFORD] Artistic roller skating is not yet recognised as an Olympic sport, which Besford said she wanted to put under the spotlight in her exhibition. GB Skate Artistic, Britain's governing body , said not being an Olympic sport meant it struggled to gain funding, adding that it believed every nation was striving to see it one day get accepted. Skate Norfolk runs sessions for children and adults across the county and said roller skating was much more popular than it was 10 years ago. "We are busy, we just do not have enough volunteers to run more sessions," said a spokesperson. Besford said it was amazing to see the skaters over the past year, and how skating has shaped their lives [EDD SMITH/BBC] Speaking about her photography, Besford said she wanted to remove the skaters from the intensity of the rink and portray them in everyday life in their bedrooms, alongside their array of medals and trophies. She has seen them all grow from young teenagers into adulthood. "They're all doing incredibly well, with going to university, having careers," she said. "Their connection with the sport has very much influenced in the way that they think, and the way they believe in themselves as young adults now." The madness started early on a crucial second-down play at the ASU 1-yard line . BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier fumbled the snap, and the referees originally blew the play dead, saying his forward progress had stopped. But then, the Big 12 replay booth stepped in and went into overdrive. After looking at the replay once, they changed the ball placement. Then they looked at it again and decided BYU running back Sione Moa had recovered the ball and scored a touchdown. It looked like a great moment for BYU, but there was just one huge problem: the booth forgot the actual rules. item.description: © David Frerker-Imagn Images Padres relief pitcher Wandy Peralta opts into $4.5 million 2027 option appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Diego Padres will have Wandy Peralta back in their bullpen next season, as the veteran left-hander has opted into the final year of his contract worth roughly $4.5 million for 2027. The 35-year-old exercised his $4.45 million player option for 2027, according to Jon Heyman of the New York Post. The decision keeps him in San Diego for one more season rather than testing the free-agent market this winter. Peralta originally signed a four-year, $16.5 million deal with the Padres in January 2024 after spending three seasons with the New York Yankees. The contract included three opt-outs, giving the reliever a chance to walk away after each of the first three seasons. He opted in after the 2024 and 2025 campaigns , and he has now done the same one last time. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The southpaw remained a durable presence for San Diego in 2026. Peralta made 65 appearances and went 3-3 with a 3.61 ERA, four holds and 50 strikeouts across 77 1/3 innings, the most innings he has logged in a Padres uniform. That followed a 2025 campaign in which he went 6-1 with a 3.14 ERA in 71 games. It was a tale of two halves for the lefty. Peralta was one of the most reliable arms in the bullpen through the first few months of the season, carrying a sparkling 2.32 ERA into late July. His strong play even made him a subject of trade talks ahead of the deadline, with Heyman reporting at the time that Peralta was “actively being discussed in trades.” The Padres ultimately held onto him through the Aug. 3 deadline, but Peralta struggled down the stretch as his ERA climbed over the final two months. San Diego’s season came to an end in the National League Division Series , where the Padres fell to the Milwaukee Brewers, who went on to win the first World Series title in franchise history. Peralta’s decision to opt in comes as little surprise. At his age and coming off an uneven season, a guaranteed salary of $4.45 million is likely more than he could have expected to land on the open market. For the Padres, bringing back Peralta gives the club a proven, experienced left-handed option in the bullpen at a reasonable price as it looks to make another postseason push in 2027. item.title: ‘Kicked us out’- Kadarius Toney slams NCAA after being ejected with 1-year-old son
item.description: Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images Former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Kadarius Toney has criticised the NCAA after claiming he and his one-year-old son were kicked out of a game over sideline access. The two-time Super Bowl champion shared his frustration on Instagram, questioning why his toddler was not allowed to remain with him despite his claim that he had a sideline pass. Toney did not identify the game he attended, leaving it unclear which institution’s access rules were involved. Kadarius Toney’s complaint raises questions over NCAA sideline rules In his Instagram story, Toney accused the NCAA of treating him unfairly and expressed frustration at being removed alongside his young son. “@ncaa K**** a*……..kicked us out the game talm bout my son Kant be on the sideline……when I [clearly] gotta sideline pass ….we talkin about a 1 yr old here🤥🤥🤥🤥🤥🤥🤥…..::and y’all wonder why ion f* m**” However, sideline credentials do not necessarily allow children of every age to enter restricted areas. It is also unclear whether Toney had secured a pass for his son or only for himself. The 2025-26 SEC Commissioner’s Regulations state that non-working personnel inside the team bench area should be at least 10 years old, while working personnel outside that area should be at least 16. Individual institutions can also impose their own restrictions. LSU requires anyone in the team bench area to be at least 10, while Georgia Southern’s media policy prohibits sideline credentials for anyone under 18. Florida, Toney’s alma mater, has similar age requirements. With his son just one year old, the toddler would fall below the minimum age under each of those policies. Toney is not the first football player to complain about being prevented from bringing a child onto the field. Former Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Chris McCain described a similar incident at Gillette Stadium in 2017, when a security guard stopped him from taking a child onto the field without the required credentials. The controversy comes after a turbulent period in Toney’s football career. The New York Giants selected him 20th overall in the 2021 NFL Draft before trading him to Kansas City in 2022. He helped the Chiefs win Super Bowl LVII, recording a touchdown reception and a 65-yard punt return against the Philadelphia Eagles. Toney later joined the Cleveland Browns, who waived him in 2024, and he has been away from the NFL since. Toney has maintained that he is not finished playing football. For now, however, his latest public dispute centres on a sideline policy rather than a potential return to the league. item.title: Seahawks Issued Trade Deadline Take Amid Jonathan Taylor Speculation
item.description: (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks were one of the teams that got the ball rolling in making big trades ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline as they traded a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick to the Indianapolis Colts for guard Quenton Nelson. Nonetheless, given that the Seahawks are in a competitive division and conference, should they make another move that can solidify them as one of, if not the best team, in the conference? Seattle Sports’ Mike Salk weighed in on whether Seattle should be looking to make one more big move in the next handful of days to bolster any weakness on the team. “Do they need one more move to get them over the top in what promises to be a very good division and also a very good conference? My answer is not yet,” Salk said in an Oct. 31 video . “Could they? Maybe. “But I would want to see exactly what it looks like with Zach Charbonnet and/or Jadarian Price back before I went out and traded for another running back. It’s an awkward fit. Charbonnet is a good player when he’s healthy .” Seahawks Don’t Need Another Running Back Although there are some takes that want the Seahawks to pursue Colts’ Jonathan Taylor to give them a bona fide RB1, Salk doesn’t see that position as a serious need, and if Seattle were to make another move, it should be on defense. “Jadarian Price looked like he had exactly the skill set that they thought he did, and if he could hang on to the ball, he may be the explosive complement to Charbonnet that they need,” Salk added. “I don’t need to see them go out and spend more assets and resources on another running back unless I know one or both of those guys aren’t going to be able to do the job. “They’ve got two weeks now to try to figure that out before the trade deadline. If they want to make a move anywhere else, quite frankly, I would rather see it be somewhere on defense. Continue to shore up the best part of this team and make it even better. Maybe that’s an extra pass rusher. Maybe that’s another cornerback, somebody for depth. But I gotta tell you, I don’t need to see them do anything right now.” Richard Sherman Urges Seattle to Pursue Jonathan Taylor Meanwhile, one person who would like for Seattle to make that move for Taylor would be former Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman. “I think a team they’ve already made a trade with, the Seattle Seahawks, would be in the mix for Jonathan Taylor as well,” Sherman said in an Oct. 29 video from “The Richard Sherman Podcast.” “I’m sure John Schneider and Ed Dodds are having those conversations right now about what it would take. “I’m guessing it would take a Day 1 pick and maybe a little bit more to get Jonathan Taylor out of Indianapolis. He’s the guy who could help this team the most. Everybody needs great running backs, but they need one really badly.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Seahawks Issued Trade Deadline Take Amid Jonathan Taylor Speculation appeared first on HEA

item.title: 'I'm tired of that': Tyrese Maxey says he wants the 76ers to stop doing one thing immediately
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers have become the comeback kings of the NBA this season. The Sixers have won five of their first six regular-season games, the latest coming against the Charlotte Hornets on Halloween night at the Spectrum Center. Every one of those victories has been spectacular because the 76ers were down on points in those games and looked like they were going to lose. That shows elite mentality, but Tyrese Maxey wants his side to stop making it so difficult for themselves. Tyrese Maxey says he’s tired of coming from behind in 76ers games The Philadelphia 76ers have been the comeback kings since the opening night of the new NBA season. Against the New York Knicks, the Sixers were 10 points down at one stage but came back to win 106-100 in the end. Then, against the Cleveland Cavaliers, they overcame a franchise-record 29-point deficit to win by eight. The wins against the Bucks and the Pacers saw the 76ers behind by seven and 13 points respectively too, which shows that their comeback victories aren’t just down to luck. That was once again evident against the Hornets on Halloween night, as Philly came from behind once again to win the game 109-104. After the win, Maxey was asked about the resilience his side has been showing. He replied on NBCS Philly: “I don’t want to do that. I’m tired of that! “This group has fighters, man. We went up, went down, came back. We’re very competitive. The game is not over until it’s over. That’s what I like about this team.” Having the ability to come from behind and win games even when it looks like there is no hope is probably the best trait to have in basketball. However, the Sixers have enough quality on their side to not go down on points in the first place, which is exactly why Maxey is right to say that he doesn’t want to do this anymore. item.title: Man United make immediate managerial decision after Chelsea defeat
item.description: Man United make immediate managerial decision after Chelsea defeat Manchester United find themselves level on points with Crystal Palace, who are in the relegation zone, after their 2-0 defeat at Chelsea. United have not been in the bottom three after August since November 1986, and yet Michael Carrick said there is no stigma attached to the Red Devils dropping into the relegation zone. What is worrying for United fans is that the club’s hierarchy seem to have the same loser’s mentality, if the report of their managerial plans is to be believed. Manchester United make “immediate decision” on Michael Carrick’s future According to talkSPORT , Michael Carrick is expected to be in the Manchester United dugout against AS Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday. It is claimed United are “highly unlikely” to make a head coach change until the upcoming international break at the earliest, “even though the hierarchy held summit talks.” United have just one win in their first nine Premier League games and sit 17th in the table, yet senior boardroom figures are still hoping Carrick can turn around the club’s form. Accordingly, Carrick is preparing to be in charge for the clash against Roma at Old Trafford. United have one win in three European outings so far this term. After that, the Mancunians are scheduled to face Aston Villa, who may push them into the relegation zone, given how well-drilled the Unai Emery-led side is. What Man United intended to do after Bournemouth defeat Following another embarrassing result, The Athletic’s Laurie Whitwell also shed light on the thinking of United’s “best-in-class” executives. It is reported that United’s hierarchy “privately pledged” to try to get to the November international break before having to act on the current head coach’s position during crisis talks after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth. In recent days, United have been strongly linked with Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte. As such, it is not far-fetched to assume they may have already started talks with potential candidates with the aim of bringing their preferred choice to the helm in November. At the same time, given how lacklustre and incompetent Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have acted in their respective roles so far, it is possible nothing concrete is being done behind the scenes.
